proof_nl:
Let d = x - j/n. Since x \ge j/n, subtracting j/n from both sides gives d \ge 0. Also, since x < (j+1)/n = j/n + 1/n, subtracting j/n gives d < 1/n. Hence 0 \le d < 1/n.

By the definition of d, we have x = j/n + d. Since J_{n,j}(d) is defined to be j/n + d, it follows that x = J_{n,j}(d).

This proves the statement.
solver_summary: From d = x - j/n, the interval condition on x immediately gives 0 <= d < 1/n by subtraction, and the definition of d gives x = j/n + d = J_{n,j}(d).
vetter_reason: The proof directly derives 0 <= d < 1/n from the interval hypothesis and then uses the definition d = x - j/n to conclude x = j/n + d = J_{n,j}(d). This matches the lemma statement exactly and uses only allowed local definitions.
